questions.question: In rain or fog, drivers should use their:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off water and snow, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Which substances can affect driving ability?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair driving, including tranquilizers, sedatives, over-the-counter cough syrups, cold tablets, allergy medications, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending. Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic pass before turning.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle when:

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
There is a solid line next to your lane.
There is a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross it to change lanes. A solid line means you cannot pass. Only pass when it is safe.

questions.question: Changing lanes is best done:

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Gradually and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and carefully. Change lanes only when necessary, as each lane change increases accident risk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness and concentration.
Reaction time and coordination.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs slow your nervous system. They reduce alertness, lower concentration, increase reaction time, and greatly reduce coordination.

questions.question: A school bus ahead has red lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop and go when you think children have exited.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop while the red lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop while the red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. Exception: You do not need to stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: If a traffic light is green but a police officer signals you to stop, you should:

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic signal.
Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions, even if they conflict with traffic signals or laws.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, what should you do?

options.text: You should still wear seat belts.
You do not need to wear seat belts.
You should wear seat belts behind your back.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should still wear seat belts.
questions.explanation: Airbags help protect you in crashes. For the best protection, always wear both your lap and shoulder belts together with airbags.

questions.question: A truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus.
Wait for the truck or bus to finish turning before you turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the truck or bus to finish turning before you turn.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit your car between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus has finished turning before you turn.

questions.question: Which statement is true about railroad crossings?

options.text: You should use cruise control near a railroad crossing to keep a steady speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal tells you to. Be careful when driving near railroad tracks.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time helps your body get rid of alcohol. Eating and drinking cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: Which of the following causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Driving faster than the speed limit or too fast for the conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Looking around and paying attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving faster than the speed limit or too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions cause many crashes. Always drive at a safe speed with the flow of traffic and within the legal speed limit.

questions.question: What should you do if you meet an aggressive driver?

options.text: Challenge them.
Get out of their way.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of their way.
questions.explanation: The safest thing to do with an aggressive driver is get out of their way. Do not try to compete with other drivers. Be respectful and cooperative on the road.

questions.question: When you take medicine, what should you do?

options.text: Ask your doctor if it is safe to drive.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor if it is safe to drive.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your ability to drive. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about how any medicine might affect your driving. This is especially important for tranquilizers and sedatives.

questions.question: Why is night driving difficult?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because you cannot see as far. Reduced visibility makes it difficult to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are going. You can only see as far as your headlights shine.

questions.question: Your vehicle has a mechanical problem. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, get it off the road and away from traffic if you can. Turn on your emergency flashers so other drivers can see you.

questions.question: You reach a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Drive around the gates if you do not see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when the gates lift.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when the gates lift.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when signs, warning devices, or flaggers warn you of a train. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Make you a better driver.
Make you feel better.
Hurt your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hurt your judgment.
questions.explanation: Not enough sleep causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and hurts your judgment.

questions.question: When should drivers let pedestrians in a crosswalk go first?

options.text: Only if pedestrians wave at you first.
Only if pedestrians are not texting.
Always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely at a crosswalk to let any car or pedestrian cross first. You can carefully drive forward only when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: If you see animals near the road while driving:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and drive carefully.
Quickly move to the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: Slow down and drive carefully if you see animals near the road. They may suddenly run or change direction. Animals often travel in groups, so more may be nearby but out of sight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road work ahead.
The road curves left then right ahead.
The road curves right then left ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right then left ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road ahead will curve right, then curve left. Slow down to safely handle the curves.

questions.question: Speeding too fast:

options.text: Saves time and gets you there faster.
Helps you avoid obstacles.
Increases the chance of serious injury or death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the chance of serious injury or death.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of car crashes. Speeding does not save time and often leads to dangerous driving decisions.
